title: improve: separate conversation behavior and tool bindings in generated instructions
body:
Related: #189522

## What Problem This Solves

Conversation participation/delivery guidance and current tool bindings have no subsection labels, so generated instructions leave them under the preceding Message Context or optional Delivery Format heading.

## User Impact

Generated prompts distinguish metadata, formatting, conversation behavior and tool availability. This is a prompt-structure correction, not a new rule or a change to routing, tool permissions or configuration; no migration is required. No improvement in model quality or instruction compliance is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

#189522 made the current conversation-instructions block explicit. Its contents still mix distinct responsibilities: trusted metadata has `### Message Context`, and a channel can add `### Delivery Format`, but neither the chat guidance nor the binding list starts a peer section. When the formatting contract is present, unrelated conversation guidance appears to continue that section.

Add `### Conversation Behavior` before the existing shared direct/group/channel guidance, and `### Tool Bindings` before the Codex wrapper's existing binding list. Group activation remains with conversation behavior. Keep Message Context because it identifies the metadata/trust boundary; deleting it would not resolve the optional Delivery Format inconsistency.

All existing instruction prose, section order, outer delimiters and supersession wording remain unchanged, including the warning that accepted tool declarations do not grant execution. Unknown chat types still produce no empty behavior section.

```text
Message Context
Delivery Format       (only when supplied by the channel)
Conversation Behavior (when source-conversation guidance exists)
Tool Bindings
```

## Evidence

Candidate: `78293322e1cc57193702add3f1e57f17a6522237`, based on `8830ff6d8ed6bbbc0ec15698428a7fcaaeb38deb`.

- Fresh live proof on the exact candidate passed through ordinary synthetic-channel inbound dispatch, an isolated real Gateway, native Codex 0.164.0 and an authenticated configured OpenAI model. Outgoing provider requests contain Message Context / Conversation Behavior / Tool Bindings for the direct case, and additionally Delivery Format for the formatted group case. Group activation stays under Conversation Behavior; the binding warning stays under Tool Bindings. Both native turns completed and delivered the expected formatting/persona/project markers locally.
- The package includes exact captured conversation blocks, an independently passing offline evidence checker, and the executed reproducer. Final live run: exit 0, 156.05 seconds including cold compilation. Two earlier harness-accounting failures are disclosed with their original evidence; neither required a product change. Additional native-thread activity is recorded rather than incorrectly counted as another source request.

- The composed delivery-format regression failed before the fix because Conversation Behavior was missing, then passed with it. All 76 focused cases across six existing test files passed, including shared chat variants, synthetic session preparation, prefix stability and Codex continuation. Combined wall time was 443.87 seconds, including cold compilation; upstream CI has not run for this draft.
- Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, the six-file generated snapshot consistency check and the test-line ratchet passed. The seven added regression lines extend existing tests; the matching per-change allocation leaves the shared baseline unchanged.
- `pnpm build:runtime` exited 0 on the exact candidate. Current core/runtime input signatures and all 188 stamped Codex output hashes were verified. The build also emitted Control UI CSS-budget warnings on untouched UI code; those warnings are recorded in the package rather than presented as a clean budget check.

Evidence package: [openclaw-conversation-headings-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34681880/openclaw-conversation-headings-evidence.zip), containing the executed reproducer, selected captures, provenance, prior validation summary and verification limits. The before excerpt is an earlier recorded runtime diagnostic, not a fresh provider-wire baseline; this is not a semantic A/B experiment. No production service or external channel delivery was changed.
